requirements.title: Data transfer termination occurs under the listed format, list, status, separator, and nonadvancing conditions
requirements.definition: Termination of a data transfer statement occurs when one of the listed conditions is reached: exhausted item or namelist lists, specified format/list separators, error, end-of-file, or nonadvancing end-of-record.

pending.format-colon-or-data-edit-no-items-termi: Use a formatted internal or named-file transfer with more format descriptors than output items and sentinel-filled output; assert only that transfer stops after the last item and leaves following sentinel storage untouched.
pending.unformatted-or-list-directed-exhaustion-: Use list-directed or unformatted sequential transfer with a finite item list initialized to distinct sentinels and surrounding records; assert successful termination after the list is exhausted without consuming a following record.
pending.namelist-output-exhaustion-terminates: Use a namelist group with known nondefault values and an output record prefilled with sentinels; assert that all group objects are represented and no additional object is required.
pending.error-condition-terminates-transfer: Use a future controlled data-transfer error that is attributable to its owning rule; observe only nonzero IOSTAT or a named status constant and never compare IOMSG text or a processor numeric code.
pending.end-of-file-condition-terminates-transfe: Create a named sequential file with known records followed by an endfile record; read with a sentinel target until a portable end condition is observed, proving transfer termination without relying on marker bytes.
pending.slash-separator-terminates-list-or-namel: Read list-directed or namelist input containing a slash after a nondefault first value and before sentinel-protected later values; assert the first target changed and later targets retain their pre-read sentinels.
pending.nonadvancing-eor-terminates-transfer: Use nonadvancing input on a known short record into a nonblank sentinel buffer; observe the portable EOR status and changed prefix only, with the next record used to show no further transfer occurred.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by creating a named external file with known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or using a conforming labelled control path) and then observe only portable properties: exact record values, successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT or named status values where the standard names them, required diagnosis of a numbered syntax rule or constraint, or file existence/position effects fixed by the source. Processor-dependent unit numbers, file encodings, buffering, timing, interprocess visibility, IOMSG text, and specific numeric status values are not asserted.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Source accounting only. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Negative plans are source-control plans unless this unit itself is a numbered syntax rule or numbered constraint, or otherwise requires rejection and a future fixture can observe the rejection portably. IOMSG wording and processor-dependent numeric status values are never an oracle; unnumbered program restrictions are not promoted to required diagnostics.
requirements.dependencies: Registered dependencies: clauses 6, 8, 9, 10, and 11 for source form, labels, names, expressions, variables, execution constructs, and existing declaration/execution foundations. Unregistered dependencies explicitly retained: earlier and later clause 12 connection, file-existence, access-mode, asynchronous-transfer, wait, status, and file-position rules; clause 13 formatting and value-separator rules; clause 15 defined I/O; clause 16 inquiry and ISO_FORTRAN_ENV status constants where future fixtures need them; clauses 3, 5, 14, 17, 18, and 19 where terminology, constants, images, IEEE support, deleted features, or scope/lifetime controls are reached.

accounting.rationale: Lists the conditions that terminate a data transfer statement.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.6.5-12.9: termination of data transfer, WAIT, BACKSPACE, ENDFILE, REWIND and FLUSH (batch164). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across two rounds. Round 1 found the portable WAIT no-operation cases missing - WAIT with ID=0 (explicitly permitted by 12.7.2 p3) and with ID= omitted on an asynchronous connection with nothing pending must succeed with IOSTAT zero - and an ENDFILE position plan that used REWIND, destroying the state under test; ENDFILE is now observed by the BACKSPACE that 12.8.3 p2 requires before the next transfer, after which a READ must report IOSTAT_END. Seventeen numbered rules were pre-accounted. Source accounting only.
